title: Cristiano Ronaldo Announces International Retirement After 23 Years with Portugal
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo announces his retirement from international football after 23 years with Portugal, ending his national team career with 234 appearances and 146 goals.
image_credit: Image: Cristiano Ronaldo waves to fans after losing the 2026 World Cup round of 16 football match between Portugal and Spain on July 6, 2026. (AFP/File)
body:
LISBON, November 5, 2026: Portuguese football superstar Cristiano Ronaldo has announced his retirement from international football, bringing an end to his 23-year career with the Portugal national team.

The Portuguese Football Federation confirmed his departure on November 5. Ronaldo leaves international football with an extraordinary record of 234 appearances and 146 goals for Portugal.

**Emotional Farewell Message**

In his farewell message, Ronaldo expressed gratitude to supporters, teammates, coaches and his family for their continued support throughout his international career.

In an English translation of his message, he said: “Thank you for these 23 years. Thank you for believing in me.”

**International Career Comes to an End**

Ronaldo made his senior international debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to become the country's most-capped player and all-time leading international goalscorer.

His retirement marks the end of a remarkable chapter in Portuguese football history.

However, the announcement concerns only his international career with Portugal and does not indicate retirement from professional club football.
